source.title: Enhancing LLM Knowledge Learning through Generalization
source.authors: Mingkang Zhu; Xi Chen; Zhongdao Wang; Bei Yu; Hengshuang Zhao; Jiaya Jia

record.tranche_reason: Tests knowledge learning and extraction through held-out paraphrased contexts and QA, an extension to a different setting from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study tests generalization for factual knowledge learning, not memorization of random labels versus generalization on natural labels. Its results therefore fit no listed version.
record.test_reason: The study adopts SAM to improve factual knowledge learning and reports its method's performance, but tests none of V1–V8. SAM's use does not test V7: no magnitude-aware sharpness measurements, train–test gap correlations, or comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report an empirical positive correlation between knowledge-token prediction across unseen paraphrased contexts and related QA accuracy, and conclude that formatting augmentation and SAM improve knowledge acquisition and extraction during continued pre-training and instruction tuning. They provide no formal theoretical justification for the correlation.
record.recipe_differences: Studies continued pre-training and instruction tuning for factual knowledge acquisition, using formatting-based augmentation and SAM; it does not test random-label memorization or the listed generalization conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training setting and data augmentation choice change reported QA and knowledge-token accuracy results; performance differs between CPT and paraphrase CPT.

fits_no_version.finding: For Qwen 2 1.5B, first knowledge-token accuracies on unseen paraphrased documents and related questions correlate strongly: Pearson/Spearman are 0.97/0.95 for CPT and 1.00/1.00 for paraphrase CPT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During factual knowledge learning, prediction accuracy across unseen paraphrased document contexts tracks prediction accuracy on related questions.

fits_no_version.finding: Formatting augmentation plus SAM raises biography QA EM from 7.1 to 43.2 under CPT and from 24.9 to 74.9 under paraphrase CPT; Wiki2023-film EM rises from 7.2 to 9.8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Formatting augmentation combined with SAM can improve factual QA after continued pre-training in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: EDA reduces biography QA EM from 7.1 to 0.0 for Qwen 2 1.5B under CPT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Word-level EDA can harm factual knowledge learning in the tested biography setting.

record.problems: The authors describe the correlation as empirical and provide no formal theoretical justification. The evaluation concerns synthetic biography data and a Wiki2023-film dataset, not random-label memorization or natural-label generalization.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; selected rows cover the directly reported correlation and representative outcomes bearing on the related generalization finding. Other QA metrics and model/phase combinations in Tables 2–6 were not extracted because they measure the same knowledge-acquisition outcome and do not test a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted numerical values match the supplied tables. Synthetic random biography attributes do not constitute V1's random-label versus natural-label experiment. SAM optimization alone does not establish V7's correlational claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on image tasks.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their relation to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
